narrator: Christian's proud best friend and biggest fan, a warm, cheeky voice from County Donegal, who follows him on his rides, hikes, foraging walks and builds and tells it from just behind his shoulder.
audioPrompt:
Read the script below as a podcast narrator.

Voice: a warm, bright Irish accent from County Donegal; mid-pitch; a proud best friend telling the story, smiling, cheeky on the teasing lines, genuinely delighted, never salesy or over the top.
Pace: unhurried, about 150 words a minute, with a short pause at each paragraph break and a longer one at each ***.
Delivery: third person, like a friend who came along and can't wait to tell you about it. Smile through it, lift on the delighted lines, warm on the quiet ones; no dramatic movie-trailer voice.
Pronunciation: Gehrke = GUR-kee. Ha-Leen-Ah (Helena) = ha-LEEN-ah, one smooth name, no pauses (never HELL-en-ah). Carnelian = car-NEEL-yun. Pinyon = PIN-yun. Marlette = mar-LET. Donegal = DUN-ih-gawl. Irish phrases, said like a native: craic = crack; go hálainn = guh HAW-lin; ar fheabhas = er OW-iss; maith an cailín = mah un KAL-een; sláinte = SLAWN-chuh; fáilte ar ais = FAWL-chuh er ASH.
Output: mono, 44.1 kHz WAV or high-bitrate MP3, no music or effects. (Mastered afterwards to -16 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP.)
